episodes.166714: On the afternoon of April 6th, a cold front made its way through West Virginia. While the majority of the area observed showers with the front, there were a few instances of strong thunderstorms. One storm in particular resulted in strong wind gusts that knocked down a tree outside the town of Ripley in Jackson County.
episodes.167207: A severe quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) moved through southeast South Carolina during the afternoon into early evening hours of April 5, 2022 as a mid-level shortwave ejected rapidly across the region in advance of a surface cold front. The environment ahead of the QLCS was favorable for severe local storms as southerly winds spread mid 60 dewpoint temperatures into a warm sector across the Southeast United States and favorable mid-level lapse rates and lifted index values helped produce mixed layer convective available potential energy (MLCAPE) as high as 1500-2000 J/kg during peak surface heating across southeast South Carolina. Within the warm sector, strong shear associated with 50-70 knot low and mid-level jets beneath the left front quadrant of a 120 knot upper-level jet, 0-6 km bulk shear around 50 knots, and 0-3 km storm relative helicity in excess of 300 m2/s2 were supportive of well organized convection and potentially embedded supercell thunderstorms in a QLCS capable of producing a prolonged path of damaging winds and strong long-track tornadoes. As the QLCS swept through southeast South Carolina, a few discrete supercell thunderstorms became exceptionally strong near or just ahead of the main line of thunderstorms, producing damaging winds, moderate size hail, and strong tornadoes.||A total of 5 confirmed tornadoes occurred across southeast South Carolina in the Charleston County Warning Area, including two long track EF-3 tornadoes, one which developed in Allendale County southwest of Allendale, SC and ended near Sycamore, SC with an approximately 13.3 mile path, and a second tornado which began in Allendale County near Ulmar, SC, then crossed into the Columbia County Warning Area in Bamberg County at peak strength, before continuing and ending in Orangeburg County with an approximately 34.8 mile path. The South Carolina Forestry Commission estimated 3,389 forest acres damaged by strong winds and tornadoes in Allendale County alone during the severe weather outbreak.
episodes.167208: A severe quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) moved through coastal waters during afternoon and evening hours of April 5, 2022 as a mid-level shortwave ejected rapidly across the region in advance of a surface cold front. The environment ahead of the QLCS was favorable for severe local storms as southerly winds spread mid 60 dewpoint temperatures into a warm sector across the Southeast United States and favorable mid-level lapse rates and lifted index values helped produce mixed layer convective available potential energy (MLCAPE) as high as 1500-2000 J/kg during peak surface heating across coastal waters. Within the warm sector, strong shear associated with 50-70 knot low and mid-level jets beneath the left front quadrant of a 120 knot upper-level jet, 0-6 km bulk shear around 50 knots, and 0-3 km storm relative helicity in excess of 300 m2/s2 were supportive of well organized convection and potentially embedded supercell thunderstorms in a QLCS capable of producing a prolonged path of damaging winds and strong long-track waterspouts. As the QLCS swept through coastal waters, numerous thunderstorms were exceptionally strong with severe winds recorded/measured near or just ahead of the main line of thunderstorms.
episodes.167454: A broken line of storms moved from west to east across East Tennessee, with some of the storms producing large hail.
episodes.167459: Strong deep-layered forcing and modest warm air advection under the left exit region of a 150 kt upper-level jet led to an environment displaying mixed layered convective available potential energy (MLCAPE) between 1500-1800 J/kg, enhanced downdraft CAPE (DCAPE), and upper 60 to lower 70 surface dewpoint temperatures supportive of vigorous thunderstorms late afternoon into evening hours. Heading into early evening hours, numerous thunderstorms developed across the local area, initially producing hail and damaging winds well ahead of a strengthening quasi-liner convective system (QLCS) well inland. As the QLCS tracked across southeast South Carolina during late evening hours, shear profiles were supportive of embedded supercell thunderstorms capable of producing damaging straight-line winds within bowing line segments (rear inflow jet) and tornadoes near bookend vortices.
episodes.167577: A few severe thunderstorms developed ahead of and along a cold front that traversed the Mid-South on 04/06/2022 producing hail and damaging wind.
episodes.167580: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a cold front associated with an occluded area of low pressure that moved into the central Great Lakes region. One storm produced damaging winds of 60 mph and nickel size hail near and west of the Fort Payne community.
episodes.167635: As a cold front moved through the forecast area, storms developed along it. A few of the storms became severe with reports of large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.167832: A few rounds of rain and thunderstorms moved across different parts of the state through the 6th of the month. On the 6th, thunderstorms with large hail moved across northwest Arkansas.
episodes.167994: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over northwestern Arkansas during the late evening of the 5th, as a cold front moved through the area. The strongest storms produced large hail up to quarter size.
episodes.168298: Heavy rain brought flooding to a couple of rivers in the early part of April.
episodes.168648: A warm and moist SW wind flow across the South Florida led to the formation of thunderstorms across Palm Beach County during the afternoon hours of April 6th. One of these thunderstorms produced a tornado in Palm Beach Gardens. Lightning from these storms triggered a brush fire near PGA Boulevard and the Florida Turnpike.
episodes.168649: A warm and moist SW wind flow across the South Florida led to the formation of thunderstorms across Palm Beach County during the afternoon hours of April 6th. One of these thunderstorms produced a tornado in Palm Beach Gardens, and a waterspout just off the coast.
episodes.168692: An upper-level disturbance moved across the Deep South in the early morning hours of April 5, 2022. This fostered the development of a surface low which moved across Central Mississippi and into North Alabama.  Thunderstorms in the morning initially posed a threat of large hail and damaging winds.  Later in the morning and into the afternoon, storms became more surface-based and a tornado threat resulted, mainly impacting the southern and southeastern portions of Central Alabama. On April 6th, a strong cold front moved through Alabama, producing another round of severe thunderstorms, but no tornadoes.
episodes.168825: A very strong occluded low pressure system was making its way across the Upper Midwest during the day, Wednesday April 6, as the occluded front passed through the Ohio Valley. The associated cold and warm front then emerged across the state of Kentucky, with a quick one-two punch as the warm front moved through the eastern half of the state in the afternoon, and the cold front quickly followed in the evening. Multiple bands of showers and thunderstorms moved through eastern Kentucky during the evening hours on April 6 as a result of these two systems. While most storms were below severe limits, one storm developed in south-central Kentucky, and continue to gain strength as it progressed eastward throughout the afternoon. By the time it reached Laurel County, it began to bow outwards, with strong winds presenting themselves on the front edge of the storm. These winds were maximized along a path in the communities of Wood Creek Lake, Hare, and East Bernstadt, all just northwest of the county center of London.
episodes.168832: A multi-day severe weather outbreak initiated with a warm moist air mass situated over Georgia as a strengthening upper level system pushed across central Georgia. With moderate instability in place with increased shear, combined to create numerous severe thunderstorms, taking the form of a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) with several strong supercells ahead of the front.  The resulting front stalled across central Georgia and interacted with a weaker shortwave moving up from the Gulf of Mexico, serving as a catalyst for another day of severe weather and flash flooding on April 6th.
episodes.169143: A strong thunderstorm that was certainly capable of producing a tornado moved through Cooper County, and caused isolated damage. While this damage was not confirmed to be a tornado, it's plausible this storm could have produced a brief tornado as it pushed through the county.

A tornado developed from a south-moving thunderstorm over northern Palm Beach County. The tornado touched down in the area of Burns Road in Palm Beach Gardens, producing roof, awning, and fence damage to an apartment complex and adjacent community center. There was substantial damage at the community center to light poles, fences, bleachers, pool equipment, and playground equipment. The tornado then passed over the property of Palm Beach Gardens High School where a wind gust of 78 mph was recorded. Damage at the school was primarily to trees and fences. The tornado continued to produce tree damage along Military Trail until lifting near the St. Ignatius Loyola Cathedral south of Holly Drive.||It was determined to be a high-end EF-0 with maximum winds estimated around 85 mph. Damage amounts were provided by Palm Beach Gardens PD and emergency management officials.
The public relayed a report via social media of quarter size hail in Summers Corner.
A wind gust of 78 mph was recorded by the Earth Networks site PLMGR at Palm Beach Gardens High School in association with the tornado which moved through the area.

A QLCS EF0 tornado quickly developed along a line of storms the evening of Wednesday April 6, 2022.  The tornado developed near the Twiggs/Bleckley County line along I-16 where several trees were snapped and uprooted.   [4/6/22: Tornado #2, County #1/3, EF-0, Twiggs/Bleckley/Laurens, 2022:022].

Continuation from Twiggs County -- The tornado path closely followed I-16 Southeastward where trees were snapped or uprooted often on one side of interstate or the other.  Radar data confirms the path and storm direction was to the ESE aligning with damage found on the ground along the interstate.  The tornado continued for over 3 miles along the interstate snapping or uprooting trees across GA Hwy 112, Eason Hill Church Rd in Laurens County before weakening and lifting as it approached GA HWY 278 southwest of the town of Montrose.  Most of the damage was confined to the area between mile markers 32 to 35 along I-16. [4/6/22: Tornado #2, County #2/3, EF-0, Twiggs/Bleckley/Laurens, 2022:022].
